subject: KMS region binding + temporary cross-region cache/backup clarifications
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@edgecloud.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@edgecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: KMS region binding + cache replication questions

Hi Chloe —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a couple of questions from security and procurement as we work the redline:

1) KMS binding: Can you confirm whether encryption keys for EU-pinned datasets can be constrained to an EU-managed key? Our DPO would like a clear statement that keys used to encrypt customer data will not be exported to non-EU regions for hosted/pinned workloads.

2) Ephemeral cache / KV replication: we understand Redwood uses KV caching for latency. Does any portion of the KV cache or prefix cache ever cross-region (e.g., temporarily replicated to US for failover/latency)? If so, under what conditions and with what controls?

3) Backups / snapshots: Are backups of model or inference metadata ever stored outside the pinned region? If so, is key wrapping used and can we get the subprocessor list for storage/DR?

We'd like short, specific answers so our Legal/Security teams can proceed with the DPA redline review. I attached a short XLS with our KMS requirements.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

—Anika
Anika Rao
Senior Security Manager, EdgeCloud Inc.
attachments: edgecloud_kms_requirements.xlsx

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS region binding + cache replication questions

Hi Anika —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus and Lauren for the technical and contractual pieces respectively. High-level answers below; Marcus and Lauren will follow with the details and a suggested DPA amendment. If you'd like, we can schedule a short Q&A tomorrow.

Summary answers (short):
- KMS binding: For EU-pinned workloads on Redwood Private or Dedicated, keys may be customer-managed (CMK) in an EU KMS and we will bind/require that key for encryption-at-rest for that account. For Redwood-hosted (standard) we offer region-residency with provider-managed keys; export of keys to non-EU regions does not occur for pinned tenants unless explicit cross-region key-wrapping is requested.
- Ephemeral cache: KV/prefix caches are in-memory (GPU/RAM) and not persisted to object storage. We do, however, have two limited cases of cross-region data movement: (1) encrypted, ephemeral cache replication for active failover under severe load, and (2) DR snapshot replication for backups — both are controlled and logged (see Marcus' note).
- Backups/snapshots: Snapshots for customer artifacts are stored encrypted. For EU-pinned customers we default to EU storage; if cross-region replication is required by configuration, keys are wrapped by the EU CMK or a region-bound wrapping key.

Lauren: can you confirm proposed DPA language (KMS-binding + temporary replication exception) and attach the redline back? Marcus: quick technical note on cache eviction, persistence, and audit logging?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS region binding + cache replication questions

Anika —

Adding the technical detail you requested. I'll keep it concise but explicit:

1) KV / prefix cache:
- Primary storage: in-memory on the serving node (GPU RAM or host RAM). These caches are not written to persistent block/object storage during normal operation.
- Replication: we have a controlled, opt-in fast-failover feature where a small portion of the active KV index (only key identifiers and encrypted prefixes, not raw customer prompt data) can be replicated to a warm standby in another region to meet an availability SLO. This replication is encrypted in transit and at rest and uses key-wrapping with the customer's EU CMK when configured.
- Eviction: caches follow an LRU policy with TTL; when a node is terminated the in-memory cache is torn down and never flushed to disk. We log cache replication events to the customer-visible audit log.

2) Backups and snapshots:
- Metadata snapshots (deployment manifests, model shards index, operational metrics) may be stored in object storage. For EU-pinned accounts we store primarily in EU buckets. Cross-region replication for DR is only enabled for customers who opt into multi-region DR; when enabled, snapshots are encrypted with a data key and the wrapping key remains in-region (we perform key-wrapping/unwrapping with the EU CMK).

3) Subprocessors: current list relevant to storage/DR: AWS eu-west-1 (S3), GCP europe-west4 (Cloud Storage), and a managed backup vendor (TapeSafe Ltd — EU partner). For any cross-border processing we run a subprocessors disclosure and can provide signed subprocessors list.

4) Auditability: All key operations, replication events, and snapshot copies are recorded in our audit service and surfaced to customers via the Console + downloadable logs. We can provide a sample audit extract for your review.

If EdgeCloud needs strict prohibition on any cross-region replication, we can set up a config to disable fast-failover and DR replication; the trade-off is a longer RTO. Happy to show the console flags.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Inference Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@edgecloud.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@edgecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS region binding + cache replication questions (DPA redline)

Hi Anika —

Thanks for the detail; I've prepared a short DPA amendment that: (a) commits to region-bound CMK usage for EU-pinned accounts where the customer provides the key, (b) defines a narrow "temporary replication" exception for active failover limited to encrypted key identifiers and prefixes (explicitly excluding full prompt/response payloads), and (c) requires prior written approval for any DR snapshot replication to a non-EU region.

I've attached the redline for your legal team to review. Key notes:
- Clause reference: Section 4.2 (Data Localization & Key Management) — amendment adds language on customer-managed keys and key wrapping for exceptions.
- Auditability: we will provide replication audit logs within 48 hours of request.
- Opt-out: customer may elect to disable fast-failover / cross-region DR in the account config.

If these items look OK, I'll prepare an amendment + DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
